JUDGMENT :
1. The present appeal under Section 96 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 challenging the judgment and decree dated 20.11.2019 passed by learned Civil Judge, Central-09, Tis Hazari Courts,
Delhi, whereby suit of the plaintiff with respect to the possession was decreed.

sentences.text: For the sake of convenience, the parties will be referred by their original status.

2. Brief case of the plaintiff, as mentioned in the plaint, can be described herein as under:-
RCA No. 157/2019 Page no. 1 of 11  2.1 Plaintiff claims himself to be owner of shops No. 74 and 75, forming part of property No. 7255, situated at Ajindra Market, Prem Nagar, Delhi-110007 (hereinafter referred to as 'the suit property'), which were let out to the defendant at a monthly rent of Rs.10,000/- for a period of 11 months commencing from 01.07.2013 vide registered rent agreement dated 26.06.2013.
It has been further stated that tenancy of the defendant came to an end in June, 2014.
However despite repeated requests the defendant failed to vacate the tenanted/suit premises.
Accordingly, a notice dated 23.06.2014, under Section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act was served upon him but despite service of said notice defendant failed to vacate the tenanted/suit premises.
Hence, plaintiff filed the present suit for possession, permanent injunction and recovery of damages/mesne profit.

sentences.text: Written Statement 3.1

It has been stated in the written statement that father of defendant is the owner and in possession of the premises in question, who is carrying on his business of grocery shop under the name and style of his Sole Proprietorship Firm M/s Man Singh Multan Singh for last more than 22 years.

It has been further stated that the prosecution was also initiated against the father of the defendant under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 on the basis of a sample lifted on 25.08.2021 from the premises in question and the father of defendant was convicted and sentenced on 30.11.2013 by the Court of Sh. Balwant Rai Bansal, ACMM, Patiala House Courts, New Delhi.
It RCA No. 157/2019 Page no. 2 of 11 has been further stated that the plaintiff is the friend of the defendant.

It has been stated that for the past some time, the relations between the defendant and his father were not good and taking the undue advantage of said bad relations of defendant with his father, the plaintiff approached the defendant and assured that he would purchase the said shop from father of defendant or otherwise would get the premises in question vacated from the father of defendant by any manner and would provide peaceful and vacant possession of premises in question to the defendant and offered the defendant the tenancy of the premises in question.

It has been further stated that believing the said false assurances and misrepresentation of the plaintiff, the rent agreement in question was executed between the parties but the said rent agreement was never acted upon as the plaintiff never handed over the possession of the premises in question to the defendant after getting it from the father of the defendant.

Hence, the said rent agreement is null,
void and illegal document.

It has been further stated that the said rent agreement therefore never acted upon and the defendant has not paid any rent to the plaintiff and the plaintiff has filed the present suit only to extract money from the defendant.
It has been further categorically stated that as such there is no relationship of landlord and tenant between the parties.

4. The decree of possession was passed vide order dated 20.11.2019 on the basis of admission of the defendant under order 12 rule 6 CPC, which has been challenged on the following grounds:-
RCA No. 157/2019 Page no. 3 of 11  (i) Ld.

Trial court has failed to apply correct principles of law as stipulated under Order 12 Rule 6 CPC (ii) Ld. Trial court erred in holding that there exists a relationship of landlord and tenant between the parties.
Though, the appellant had never admitted the respondent to be the owner of the suit property.
(iii) Ld.

Trial court has wrongly observed that there is no dispute between the parties with respect to existence of landlord and tenant relationship holding that defendant has admitted the execution of rent agreement.
(iv) Ld. Trial court erred in holding that defendant admitted that plaintiff is his landlord and he is in possession of the suit property in the capacity of tenant.

(v) Ld. Trial court ignored the specific pleadings of the appellant in para No. 1 of the preliminary objections of the written statement that plaintiff never handed over possession of the premises in question to the defendant.

Thus, the observations of Ld. Trial Court to the effect that defendant has admitted the plaintiff as his landlord and he is in possession of the suit property in the capacity of a Sunil Kumar Jain vs Mahesh Chander Gupta on 24 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175958709/
2 tenant is factually incorrect and inconsistent with the pleadings of the appellant.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (vi) Ld. Trial court erred in holding that rent agreement was executed between the parties under misrepresentation and assurances made by the plaintiff by taking undue advantage of sour relationship between defendant and his father.
RCA No. 157/2019 Page no. 4 of 11  (vii) Ld. Trial Court has failed to examine the essential facts with respect to ownership and possession of the plaintiff over the suit property.
The plaintiff,

though, heavily relied upon the said rent agreement but failed to file any document before the Ld.
Trial Court to show that he is the owner of the suit property or prior to execution of the said agreement he was in possession of the suit property.
(viii) Ld. Trial Court has overlooked the fact that plaintiff has filed on record a GPA dated 20.08.1992 purportedly executed by one Guljar Singh Randhawa in his favour.

The said GPA reflects that plaintiff had been made attorney with respect to shop No. 75 only and except the said document plaintiff has not been able to place any document to substantiate his claim of ownership and possession over the suit property.

Though, the GPA with respect to shop No. 74 is in the name of Shri Rajiv Gupta, hence he was not competent to execute the rent agreement dated 26.06.2013 with respect to shop No. 74 and the same is void-ab-initio.
(ix) Ld.
Trial court overlooked various documents filed before it by the defendant which shows that it was his father who was in possession of the suit property even prior to institution of the suit.

Ld.
Trial court also overlooked the fact that plaintiff had failed to place on record any document which would show that plaintiff never received any rent from the appellant.
5. Notice of the appeal was issued to the respondent.
RCA No. 157/2019 Page no. 5 of 11 6.
No reply to the appeal was filed.
However, it was orally argued by the counsel for the respondent that the Ld. Trial Court has rightly passed the impugned judgment / decree dated 20.11.2019.
Hence, prayer was made to dismiss the appeal with heavy costs.
7. Arguments heard at length advanced by the Ld. Counsel for appellant and the respondent.
Trial Court Record perused.
Observation on appeal 8.

Before discussing the facts in hand, the relevant law Order 12 Rule 6 CPC has been reproduced as under for easy reference:-
"ORDER XII-ADMISSIONS Rule 6. Judgment on admissions- (1) Where admissions of fact have been made either in the pleading or otherwise,
whether orally or in writing, the Court may at any stage of the suit, either on the Sunil Kumar Jain vs Mahesh Chander Gupta on 24 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175958709/
3 application of any party or of its own motion and without waiting for the determination of any other question between the parties, make such order or give such judgment as it may think fit, having regard to such admissions.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (2) Whenever a judgment is pronounced under sub-rule (1), a decree shall be drawn up in accordance with the judgment and the decree shall bear the date on which the judgment was pronounced."

9. In the case in hand, while considering the admission of the appellant / defendant, Ld. Trial Court vide order / judgment dated 20.11.2019 held as under:-
RCA No. 157/2019 Page no. 6 of 11 "(a) Existence of Landlort-Tenant Relationship - There is no dispute between the parties with respect to the existence of landlord and tenant relationship between them as the defendant has admitted the execution of registered rent agreement.

Therefore,
the defendant has admitted that plaintiff is his landlord; that he is in possession of the suit property in the capacity of a tenant and that the rent agreement dated 26.06.2013 was executed between them.

Thus, the first ingredient stands satisfied."
10.
The rent agreement relied upon by the plaintiff is of dated 26.06.2013.

The defendant has claimed the said rent agreement was got executed fraudulently by the plaintiff on misrepresentations and false assurances and actually his father is the owner and in possession of the suit property.
At first, no such ownership documents have been placed on record by the appellant.

The only document which has been relied upon by the appellant is the order of the Ld. ACMM,
Patiala House Court, District whereby his father was convicted and sentenced vide order dated 30.11.2011.

I am not convinced with the said arguments as father of the appellant was convicted and sentenced under Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 Act on the basis of the sample lifted on 25.08.2001 from the premises in question and that fact does not mean that he becomes the owner of the said property.

entities.text: Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Merely the fact that he was convicted for the adulteration of goods while having possession of the suit shop in the year 2001 does not mean that he becomes the owner by said fact.
Hence, the above said arguments falls flat.
RCA No. 157/2019 Page no. 7 of 11 11.
On the other hand, the plaintiff has relied upon two GPA which are of dated 20.08.1992.

One has been executed by Sh. Gulzar Singh Randhawa in favour of the respondent with respect to shop no.
75 and the another was executed by Sh. Gulzar Singh in favour of the son of respondent namely Rajeev Dutta with respect to the shop no.
74.
It is relevant to mention here that section 116 of Indian Contract Act creates an estoppel against the tenant from challenging the ownership of the landlord.

12. It was further contended by the Ld Counsel for appellant that the rent agreement dated 26.06.2013 is forged and fabricated as there is one more rent agreement which was executed by Mrs.
Saloni Garg in favour of Soyam Singh Chauhan with respect to the shop no.

sentences.text: Ld Counsel for appellant by pointing the above said document is making contradictory submissions.

On one hand, it has been stated by the appellant that his father is owner of the suit property and on the other hand, he has relied upon above said document alleging that Mrs. Saloni Garg is the owner.

Further, the appellant has stated that it is his father, who is in possession of the suit property though the said rent agreement reflects that some other person is in the possession of the suit property.

13. So far as the possession of the suit property is concerned, the appellant has stated that his father is in the possession of the suit RCA No. 157/2019 Page no. 8 of 11 property but he has duly executed the execution of one rent agreement dated 26.06.2013, wherein it has been categorically stated that the respondent is the actual owner and in lawful possession of the suit property and it has been rented out to the appellant.

The relevant portion of the said agreement is as under:-
"Whereas the Landlord / First Party (Sh. Mahesh Chander Gupta) is the actual owner and in lawful possession of the shop no. 74 & 75, a part of the built up property bearing no.
7255 Situated at Ajindra Market, Prem Nagar, Delhi-110007 hereinafter called the property.

And Whereas on the request of the Second Party / Tenant (Sh. Sunil Kumar Jain), the first party /
Landlord have let out the above and property to the second party / Tenant and the second party /
Tenant are desirous of taking the said property/premises on rent from the first party / landlord as for commercial purposes only.

That the monthly rent for the period of the above said premises is fixed between both the parties is Rs. 10,000/- per month excluding water and electricity (Commercial), which shall be paid by the second party / tenant to the first party / landlord in respect of the said premises / property."
14. The rent agreement dated 26.06.2013 is a registered one, execution of which has been duly admitted.
Certain photographs have also been placed on record by the plaintiff which depicts the possession of the appellant over the suit property.

15. Here, I deem it appropriate to mention the judgment passed in the case of Vijaya Myne Vs. Satya Bhusan Kaura, reported in 142 (2007) DLT 483 (DB), the Division Bench of the Hon'ble Delhi High Court has observed as under:-
RCA No. 157/2019 Page no. 9 of 11 "....... 12. The purpose and objective in enacting the provision like Order 12 Rule 6, CPC is to enable the Court to pronounce the judgment on admission when the admissions are sufficient to entitle the plaintiff to get the decree, in as much as such a provision is enacted to render speedy judgments and save the parties from going through the rigmarole of a protracted trial.

entities.text: Vijaya Myne Vs. Satya Bhusan Kaura, reported in 142 (2007) DLT 483 (DB)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The admissions can be in the pleadings or otherwise, namely in documents,
correspondence etc.
These can be oral or in writing.

The admissions can even be constructive admissions and need not be specific or expressive which can be inferred from the vague and evasive denial in the written statement while answering specific pleas raised by the plaintiff.
The admissions can even be inferred from the facts and circumstances of the case.
No doubt, for this purpose, the Sunil Kumar Jain vs Mahesh Chander Gupta on 24 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175958709/

entities.text: Sunil Kumar Jain vs Mahesh Chander Gupta on 24 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5 Court has to scrutinize the pleadings in their detail and has to come to the conclusion that the admissions are unequivocal, unqualified and unambiguous.
In the process, the Court is also required to ignore vague, evasive and unspecific denials as well as inconsistent pleas taken in the written statement and replies.
Even a contrary stand taken while arguing the matter would be required to be ignored....."
16. It is to be kept in mind that the purpose of Order XII rule 6 CPC is to confer upon the plaintiff a right to speedy judgment.
The Courts have to ensure that in an appropriate case, a party on the admission of other party can press for judgment as a matter of legal right.
The Courts should not allow a dishonest litigant to prolong the trial on the flimsy ground.

Reliance is placed upon in Vinay Kumar RCA No. 157/2019 Page no. 10 of 11 Aggarwal Vs. Radha Rani Aggarwal 2018 SCC Online Del 6534.
17.

entities.text: Aggarwal Vs. Radha Rani Aggarwal 2018 SCC Online Del 6534
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The judgment relied upon by the appellant i.e. Karan Kapoor v. Madhuri Kumar; 2022 LiveLaw (SC) 567 is differentiable in the present facts and circumstances as herein the appellant has no document to show that he became the owner of the suit property.

sentences.text: 18. In view of abovesaid reasons, it is hereby held that Ld. Trial Court has rightly appreciated the material placed on record.
The Court does not find any infirmity or irregularity in the reasoning given vide order dated 20.11.2019.
Consequently, the appeal against the Judgment/Decree dated 20.11.2019 is hereby dismissed.
The judgment dated 20.11.2019 passed by Ld. Trial court is hereby affirmed.
19. The appeal stands disposed-of accordingly.
Copy of this order be sent to the Ld. Trial Court alongwith trial court record.
20. Appeal file be consigned to Record Room after necessary Digitally signed by compliance.
